journal_diversity_policy: Within the existing Crossref source-first budget, reserve a rotating lane for configured journals with zero or one accepted A/B item. Interleave this lane with policy, Q1 and broad journal rotations so deadline truncation cannot repeatedly favour the same venues. Source diversity changes discovery attention only; ordinary European/EU, R&I and quality admission gates remain unchanged.
crossref_priority_task_order_policy: Interleave journal-query priority tasks across journals before applying the persisted cursor. The request budget is unchanged, but a partial run now touches many venues instead of spending most priority tasks on one journal.

full_text.rule: Require repeated/spread R&I and geopolitical evidence in the available full text.

abstract_only.rule: Require EU + R&I + geopolitics to be substantively connected; do not require document sections that are unavailable.

metadata_only.rule: Insufficient text is not evidence of irrelevance; attempt abstract/full-text recovery.

eu_anchor_context_rule: Bare EU is not a European Union anchor when the document explicitly defines EU as another abbreviation (for example environmental uncertainty).
matrix_evidence_rule: For vetted Strand A evidence, classify row and independence/competitiveness directions from the source-backed title/summary/relevance evidence; direction keywords support the rubric but are not a second gate. Weak signals remain event/mechanism gated.
priority_people_rule: Curated researchers receive extra discovery attention inside the ordinary scholarly rotation. Their works are not labelled, separated, or displayed differently, and admission criteria are unchanged.
priority_people_fallback_rule: If exact-author discovery yields nothing, use affiliation + topic hints for a bounded contextual scholarly query. Results from this fallback are processed exactly like all other scholarly discoveries and may belong to any researcher.
high_order_inference_feedback_policy: Persistent Level-4/5 candidates may contribute missing-link and falsifier searches inside the existing finding-context query budget. They do not increase the lane budget, bypass admission, or reduce Strand A evidence standards.
english_evidence_rule: Public A/B evidence must be an English-language publication. Explicit foreign-language metadata, a non-English publication title, or meaningful non-Latin source prose rejects the record. An English abstract does not rescue a foreign-language publication; no translation is used for admission.
eu_ri_geopolitics_core_rule: Strand A requires source-supported EU/European scope plus a substantive economic-security mechanism: dependence or supply security, industrial capacity, trade or investment exposure, technology control or leakage, critical infrastructure, coercion/leverage, or partnerships - including the trade-off between protection and openness.
material_external_shock_rule: Inference-only external-shock admission is disabled. A non-EU development can enter only when the source itself explicitly establishes a substantive effect on EU/European R&I in geopolitical/economic-security terms; it then passes through the same normal graded Europe-scope and R&I gates as every other item.
reader_point_subject_rule: Every reader-facing finding and why-it-matters point must start with an explicit actor, system or topic. Do not start with vague references such as this, these, those, it, they, such, the study, the paper, the findings or the developments.
reader_point_sentence_rule: Reader-facing points must be complete sentences of at most 120 characters. Never hard-cut a sentence and never use ellipses to force the limit.
preferred_q1_journals_note: Discovery preference only. Shortlist verified against SCImago SJR 2024 Q1 listings; quartiles can change. Never an admission requirement.
source_attention_policy: Prefer direct recent-content checks of EU primary institutions, trusted international organisations such as OECD/NATO/ESA/CERN/EPO where substantively relevant, national science bodies, research organisations, elite/priority journals and specialist R&I reporting. Prestige expands discovery attention but never bypasses graded source-supported European/EU R&I relevance, method quality, or weak-signal trust requirements.
matrix_balance_policy: Matrix coverage uses a source-supported semantic contract for every cell, including reviewed adjudications. Sparse cells get extra discovery attention across multiple plausible mechanisms; no cell is filled to satisfy a quota.
matrix_balance_rotation_rule: Coverage is recalculated every scan and during depth waves. Sparse cells receive extra searches for distinct causal mechanisms (talent, access, scale, rules) while every placement must evidence the row plus both control/dependence and performance directions.

foresight_author_followup_rule: Authors already evidenced by admitted Strand-B foresight/method publications receive a bounded rotating exact-author check in OpenAlex/Crossref. Their later works must pass the ordinary A/B gates; no institution or domain receives a permanent lane.
weak_signal_evidence_followup_rule: An interesting low-evidence C item that cites or points to research/report/publication evidence may trigger bounded link-following and scholarly search. Any stronger source is admitted separately through the ordinary A/B gates; the C item itself remains low evidence.
foresight_expert_seed_rule: Named people may receive bounded person-centric discovery attention; no domain or institution is privileged, and every discovered item must pass the ordinary EU R&I A/B gates.
citation_snowball_pinned_seed_titles: The Global Landscape of National AI Strategies
phrase_ontology_policy: A/B phrases support discovery and linkage only. C admission has two normal routes: a dated attributable European R&I development, or dated trusted analysis with a specific contradiction/reframing. A anchors are optional. Formal proposals are factual proposal events, not realised outcomes; archive/index/event-promo pages fail. No minimum C quota is used.
source_family_rotation_rule: Every ordinary scan gives institutional/EU sources and scholarly journal collectors concurrent first-class time slices. Scholarly source-first work is interleaved across policy, Q1, broad and underrepresented-journal lanes, while priority journal-query tasks are interleaved across venues. Each family keeps independent persisted cursors; no output quota is imposed and source diversity never bypasses admission.
topic_rotation_rule: The Strand-A scholarly query bank is interleaved by coarse topic family before persistent rotation, and Matrix-gap/finding-context/method lanes are round-robin interleaved into the executed prefix.
reader_quality_ranking_rule: Public analytical readers do not display or order by source-quality scores. The Stuff audit/export workbook alone carries a 0-100 technical evidence ranking combining source authority, EU relevance, evidence strength and author transparency.
scanner_eu_relevance_rule: EU relevance uses graded source-grounded scope: direct or supported may pass A; unclear/none do not. Direct covers explicit EU institutions/programmes/instruments. Supported covers substantive European R&I systems, datasets, networks, regions or multi-country frames. A single member-state name alone is not EU scope, and inference-only foreign-to-Europe bridges remain disabled.
stuff_ranking_rule: 0-100 audit/export score only: source authority max 55 + EU relevance max 25 + evidence strength max 15 + author transparency max 5. This score must not be used for Matrix placement or public-reader ordering.
source_failure_reallocation_policy: If OpenAlex or Crossref becomes unavailable/rate-limited during a scan, preserve its rotation cursor and spend a substantial bounded replacement slice on unused institutional sources plus rotating trusted-journal and broad-query discovery in the healthy scholarly family. Admission rules do not change.

news_discovery_policy: Run bounded direct-source checks for core R&I news publishers in parallel with Google News RSS. Google News is supplementary discovery, not the sole transport for configured core sources.

priority_policy_journal_watchlist_note: Source-first scholarly lane for research policy, mobility, innovation systems, geoeconomics and foresight. These venues never bypass the same European/EU + substantive R&I admission gate.
direct_top_journal_policy: Nature and Science are checked directly every ordinary scan; two additional elite journals rotate through a direct publisher-page lane. Direct journal pages can feed A/B or, when they are current developments rather than A/B evidence, the C candidate pool. No journal prestige bypasses relevance/quality gates.

external_shock_watch_rule: Possible shocks are parked separately when trusted source text has admissible source-supported EU/European R&I scope, a recognised shock family and a realised event signal but does not yet pass every strict shock test. Parked candidates never count as filed external shocks.
source_quality_admission_rule: Source quality remains upstream. Discovery searches configured trusted institutions, international organisations and high-quality scholarly venues. State-controlled media, their laundering networks, disinformation outlets and state-organ journals are hard-blocked on every route (domains, names, substrings); no prestige, curator hint or topic match overrides the block. Peer-reviewed work by authors from any country in a trusted venue is unaffected.
post_scan_reader_refresh: Every completed scan rewrites radar.json; Matrix, Risks & opportunities, Read at least this and External shocks re-derive from the refreshed corpus. Discovery first performs a full trusted-source census where transport/time allows, then query/depth lanes.
discovery_policy: Recall-first: search the full configured trusted-source universe on every run where transport/time allows. Admission still requires European/EU R&I substance; source prestige never creates relevance. Marginal but source-valid records may enter at low reader priority rather than being missed upstream.
curator_seed_discovery_policy: Curator-supplied known-good examples seed rotating adjacent searches for EU/European R&I. They never bypass source quality, direct/supported European scope, substantive R&I, or final admission checks.
crossref_source_first_depth_policy: Every priority journal checks newest contents; high-output journals that fill the first page also rotate through one deeper four-month page per scan so older-in-window articles are not permanently hidden.
main_radar_recall_policy: High recall for central European/EU research & innovation, prioritising geopolitical, geoeconomic, security, dependency, international-competition/cooperation, rules-power and talent/capability mechanisms. A bounded Tier 1/2 major EU-R&I-system route prevents zero-yield scans when strategically important system evidence is not explicitly labelled geopolitical.
source_yield_policy: Never disable, demote, or prune a configured source because of low admissions. Track metadata coverage, judgeable records, duplicates/known items and gate yield separately; metadata availability is not source quality.

evidence_product_ranking_policy: When publishable candidates compete for limited NEW slots, completed peer-reviewed papers, working papers and substantive formal/institutional reports are preferred over routine funding announcements and current-event notices. Discovery route never changes admission.
funding_notice_selection_policy: Routine grants/calls/award announcements remain eligible only when they independently pass A/B, but they do not outrank completed research evidence merely because Horizon Europe or funding is in the title.

scan_allocation_policy: Normal scans use a 45-day overlap, protect A-oriented discovery/evaluation, reserve a small protected recent-first Strand-B methods lane (with 2016-era foundational fallback), and retain bounded C/low-yield recovery. Repetitive continuation is capped; admission quality is never lowered to meet output targets.
active_core_policy: The packaged 200 A/B records are the starting baseline only. Every newly accepted A/B record remains in the public strand cumulatively; there is no 200-item replacement cap. Deduplication, admission, integrity and explicit precision cleanups still apply.
signal_anchor_policy: Strand C is an independent temporary weak-signal stream on the same EU/European R&I watch themes. A publication anchor is optional context, not an admission condition. The base retention window is 60 days, active announced/proposed/in-negotiation processes may persist for 180 days, and adopted/in-force/operating developments may persist for 365 days; retention is measured from first_seen and does not alter low-evidence status.
frontier_gap_zero_yield_policy: If the same Matrix target set produces no A/B candidates in two consecutive depth waves, stop repeating that Matrix depth lane for this run and return time to other rotating discovery families.

source_context_policy: Context-rich EU primary sources may be searched broadly; general scholarly/news discovery requires multiple independent EU/R&I/strategic dimensions. Generic terms such as Europe, innovation, technology, security, resilience or competitiveness never admit a record alone.
source_universe_note: EU-primary and high-merit scholarly/institutional sources rotate by family; source context may broaden retrieval but never weakens A/B admission.
strand_a_priority_policy: The first 20 broad scholarly query slots per source are protected for substantive Strand-A-oriented lanes when budget allows. Strand-B method queries may use remaining broad slots plus bounded method-author/source follow-up, but cannot crowd A out of the executed prefix.
high_order_inference_news_feedback_polic: Up to four missing-link/falsifier queries may join ordinary weak-signal coverage. Results still need trusted-source, 60-day and C substantive admission rules; an existing A anchor is preferred but not mandatory.
target_item_mix_rule: Relative publication balance for NEW admissions: A:C = 8:3. Strand B (methods) is disabled in this radar; methods live in the R&I radar.
c_unanchored_rule: Independent C may be admitted from a trusted source when it is a dated, concrete, source-backed external R&I/technology development capable of changing a European A state variable. The event facts must come from the source; Europe-impact language may be a clearly labelled radar inference. A publication anchor is preferred but not mandatory.
institution_rejected_reconsideration_rul: Institution fingerprints are persisted as seen only after A/B admission. Rejected, incomplete, or previously misclassified pages remain reconsiderable.
c_source_discovery_rule: Configured high-trust news and research-analysis/blog domains are queried as C discovery sources. Completed reports/studies/papers discovered there are promoted to ordinary A/B evaluation and never downgraded into C.
weak_signal_formal_proposal_rule: A PROPOSED C item is public only when a configured accountable source reports a named EU/member-state institution formally tabling/publishing/adopting a proposal/draft or launching a consultation/call for evidence. Generic plans and intentions remain precursor-only.
c_source_policy: Elite Europe-facing current reporting plus authoritative EU/international primary institutions. Broad national-media and think-tank layers are context for A/institutional discovery, not routine Strand-C publication sources.
historical_strand_policy: A+B only. Historical never searches for, reconstructs, admits, or publishes Strand C.
c_exceptional_release_rule: Bypass 8:1:3 only when something substantially happened: a realised/observed event, from a top-tier independent/specialist or authoritative primary source, with direct/supported European R&I scope (or an unusually large strategic member-state capital/control move), and one strict materiality class: major research-programme access change, binding rule/critical-access restriction, >=1bn strategic capital/control change, major strategic capability becoming operational, severe R&I access/capacity disruption, or an exceptionally large measured system shift. Proposals, consultations, warnings, commentary, calls, plans and ordinary announcements do not qualify. Exceptional C remains low-weight context and counts against future C balance.
